newsitem.title: ITALY: Marxists say could scupper Italy govt on pensions.
newsitem.headline: Marxists say could scupper Italy govt on pensions.

text.p: Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti threatened on Thursday to bring down Italy's centre-left government if it cuts state pensions.
"On pensions, we are ready to produce a crisis and the fall of the government," Bertinotti told a news conference. "Cuts to the welfare state and pensions is destructive ground for the government."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government relies on Bertinotti's party for its majority in the lower house of parliament and cannot survive without its votes.

Bertinotti delivered his warning amid debate about a government proposal to bring forward Italy's 1998 budget by four months to mid-August to send a sign of confidence on the country's ability to clean up public finances.
Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi signalled this week that he could agree to early passage of the budget if the package included structural cuts on pensions and health.
"It's up to Prodi to say whether he intends to discuss this mortal embrace or strengthen relations with (his supporters) by finishing with cuts and starting with (creating) jobs," Bertinotti said.
